title: A Guide to Basic RNA Sequencing Data Processing and Transcriptomic Analysis
author: Rowayna Shouib
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: STEP 0: Software installation Start by processing FASTQ files for quality control and further analysis of sequencing information in Terminal. Terminal is a text interface where files can be downloaded, folders created, and software installed and run using text commands. It may also be referred to as the Linux command line or Shell. In this protocol, the first phase of the analysis will be carried out using different software performed in Terminal ( steps 0–7 ), after which the analysis will transition to RStudio ( steps 8–12 ). The following link provides a resource as a primer on Terminal to understand how to create files and understand commands: https://ubuntu.com/tutorials/command-line-for-beginners#1-overview . Throughout this protocol, sample codes are provided that can be adapted to the user’s own files and folder locations. Hashtag symbols (#) denote explanations or commentaries, and any text preceded by a # is not processed as a command by Terminal or RStudio. To install appropriate software or packages, download the Bioconda package manager. Bioconda or Conda allows the installation of packages such as fastqc (used for quality control) and trimmomatic, which will be used to trim off adapter sequences and short reads of poor quality. There are a variety of different Conda formats, but in this protocol, Miniconda will be used, which can be installed and activated using: https://conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/user-guide/install/index.html . Following installation, restart Terminal. Load the Terminal app (this can be done from the start menu by typing Terminal ). Use the following code in Terminal to verify Conda has been installed: conda --version # verify conda is installed. conda update conda # update conda to latest version. y # yes when asked to proceed ([y] or n). Use the following code in Terminal to install fastqc, trimmomatic, HISAT2, Samtools, and subread (a package that includes featureCounts tool) software: conda install -y -c bioconda fastqc trimmomatic hisat2 samtools subread If prompted, an updated version of libggc may be needed. This and other packages can be found at https://anaconda.org/conda-forge/libgcc-ng , or it can be downloaded by running this script: conda install -c conda-forge libgcc-ng
MINLEN: specifies minimum length of reads (>36)

steps.title: Install Conda and required packages
steps.instruction: Download and install Miniconda, then verify with `conda --version`. Update Conda (`conda update conda` and answer y). Install FastQC, Trimmomatic, HISAT2, Samtools, and Subread (featureCounts) via `conda install -y -c bioconda fastqc trimmomatic hisat2 samtools subread`. If prompted, install libgcc-ng from conda‑forge (`conda install -c conda-forge libgcc-ng`).

steps.title: Create FASTQ working folder
steps.instruction: Make a folder for raw reads, move all FASTQ files into it, and change the Terminal working directory to that folder.

substeps.instruction: Manually move raw *.fastq (or *.fastq.gz) files into FASTQ

steps.title: Unzip FASTQ files
steps.instruction: Decompress any .gz files using gunzip; can be done file‑by‑file or with a loop.

substeps.instruction: for file in Sample_*.fastq.gz; do gunzip "$file"; done   # example loop for all files matching pattern
for file in "Sample 1_L00{1..4}_R1.fastq.gz"; do gunzip "$file"; done   # example loop for lane‑split files

steps.title: Concatenate lane‑split FASTQ files
steps.instruction: For each sample, merge files from the same read (R1 or R2) using `cat` so that each sample ends with one R1 and one R2 file.

substeps.instruction: cat Sample 1_L001_R1.fastq Sample 1_L002_R1.fastq Sample 1_L003_R1.fastq Sample 1_L004_R1.fastq > concatenated_Sample1_R1.fastq
cat Sample 1_L001_R2.fastq Sample 1_L002_R2.fastq Sample 1_L003_R2.fastq Sample 1_L004_R2.fastq > concatenated_Sample1_R2.fastq

steps.title: Run FastQC on raw reads
steps.instruction: Create a folder for QC reports and run FastQC on each concatenated FASTQ file.

steps.title: Prepare adapter file for Trimmomatic
steps.instruction: Download the appropriate adapter FASTA (e.g., TruSeq2‑PE.fa) from the Trimmomatic GitHub adapters repository, save it as plain text in the working folder.

steps.title: Trim adapters and low‑quality bases
steps.instruction: Run Trimmomatic on each sample (SE or PE) with the recommended parameters.

substeps.instruction: # To process multiple samples simultaneously, separate commands with '&' and '\' as shown in the protocol.

steps.title: Run FastQC on trimmed reads
steps.instruction: Create a folder for trimmed‑read QC and run FastQC on the paired trimmed files.

steps.title: Download genome index and align reads
steps.instruction: Obtain the HISAT2 index for the reference genome (e.g., GRCh38), unzip it, create an HISAT2 output folder, move trimmed FASTQ files and the index into that folder, then align each sample with HISAT2.

substeps.instruction: tar -xzvf grch38_genome.tar.gz   # creates folder grch38 with index files
Move concatenated trimmed FASTQ files and the grch38 folder into HISAT2
Repeat for all remaining samples or run in background with '&'

steps.title: Convert, sort, and index SAM files
steps.instruction: Using Samtools, convert each SAM to BAM, sort the BAM, and create an index.

steps.title: Count reads per gene with featureCounts
steps.instruction: Download the appropriate GTF annotation, unzip it, and run featureCounts on each sorted BAM file.

substeps.instruction: Move the GTF file into the HISAT2 folder
# -p indicates paired‑end data; -a specifies annotation; -o sets output file
Open each *.txt in Excel, keep only ‘GeneID’ and ‘Counts’ columns, save as .csv
Combine all sample count columns into a single CSV (genes in same order across samples)

steps.title: Install R packages for DESeq2 analysis
steps.instruction: In RStudio, install BiocManager, then use it to install DESeq2 and other needed packages.

steps.title: Load counts and run DESeq2
steps.instruction: Set the working directory to the folder containing the combined counts CSV, import it as a matrix, filter low‑count genes, define experimental conditions, create DESeq2 dataset, run DESeq2, and generate QC plots.

substeps.instruction: setwd("/Users/[user name]/RNASeq")   # adjust path as needed
Counts <- Counts[rowSums(Counts) > 50, ]   # keep genes with total counts >50
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = Counts, colData = coldata, design = ~condition)

steps.title: Perform pairwise comparisons and label DE genes
steps.instruction: Create result objects for each contrast, classify genes as UP/DOWN based on log2FC and p‑value thresholds, and export the labeled tables.

substeps.instruction: # Repeat for other contrasts as needed

steps.title: Generate sorted DEG list files
steps.instruction: Order DE genes by absolute log2 fold change and export tables with log2FC, p‑value, and adjusted p‑value.

substeps.instruction: write.table(data.frame(GeneID = rownames(sigs_S2_vs_S1_sorted), log2FoldChange = sigs_S2_vs_S1_sorted$log2FoldChange), file = log2FC_file_S2_vs_S1, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = TRUE)

write.table(data.frame(GeneID = rownames(sigs_S2_vs_S1_sorted), log2FoldChange = sigs_S2_vs_S1_sorted$log2FoldChange, pvalue = sigs_S2_vs_S1_sorted$pvalue, padj = sigs_S2_vs_S1_sorted$padj), file = pvalue_file_S2_vs_S1, sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = TRUE)
# Repeat for any other pairwise comparisons

steps.title: Create heatmap of DEGs
steps.instruction: Install and load the pheatmap package, select genes common to all contrasts, extract their counts, order samples, and plot & save the heatmap.

substeps.instruction: pheatmap(top_counts, scale = "row", show_rownames = FALSE, cluster_cols = FALSE, legend = TRUE, main = "Heatmap of DEGs")
pheatmap(top_counts, scale = "row", show_rownames = FALSE, cluster_cols = FALSE, legend = TRUE, main = "Heatmap of DEGs")

steps.title: Create volcano plot with gene‑set labels
steps.instruction: Install ggplot2 and ggrepel, load a gene‑set file, subset significant DE genes, label genes belonging to the set, plot the volcano, and save the figure.

substeps.instruction: # Assume diff_S2_vs_S1_gnames is the DESeq2 results data frame with a column `gene_name`
p <- ggplot(data = diff_S2_vs_S1_gnames, aes(x = log2FoldChange, y = -log10(padj), col = diffexpressed)) +
theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 13), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 13)) +
ggsave(filename = "S2_vs_S1_golgivesicle_plot.png", plot = p, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
